purpose: Close the three HRM-013 trusted callback ingress boundaries, their caller-specific authority, wire schemas, replay semantics and transport controls before any owner packet, People V61 lease or module source token is issued.

currentAuthorityIndex.rule: This carrier requires a separately validated append-only current-authority-index successor; it does not edit v1 in place.

rules: The 32768-byte limit applies to accepted request bodies and to exact APR-002 request bytes persisted in ppl_separation_waiver_request_outbox; it never expands a response limit.
Raw HRM-008 through HRM-010 callback request bytes are not persisted; only their request_body_sha256, canonical payload_sha256 and originating_payload_sha256 are durable.
Every persisted or transmitted SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 success or safe error response is capped independently at 16384 bytes.

operationNaming.rule: operation is the immutable semantic operation from the HRM-013 contract successor; sourceOperationId is the exact implementation/API operation identifier and must equal the paired bridge operationId where that bridge applies.

rules: The concrete path casePublicId and taskPublicId equal the two body fields and their signed JWT claims.
The stored task type and owner workload equal the exact caller-matrix row; a caller cannot complete another owner's task.

The first accepted ownerRevision is 1 and every later distinct accepted receipt for the same tenant, task and caller is exactly previous accepted revision plus 1; gaps and stale revisions are quarantined.
FAILED is an accepted task outcome that keeps the case in TASKS_ACTIVE; a later COMPLETED requires a new callbackEventId, the next ownerRevision and a new externalReceiptPublicId.
externalReceiptPublicId is durable callback evidence for both COMPLETED and FAILED, is persisted with the callback ledger, and is never derived from callbackEventId or the People receiptPublicId.
COMPLETED stores externalReceiptPublicId and can move the case to READY_TO_PUBLISH only when every mandatory task is COMPLETED or approval-authorized WAIVED.
Only COMPLETED for a task whose immutable template marks irreversible=true sets irreversibleAt; FAILED never does.
The concrete path casePublicId and taskPublicId equal the body and signed JWT claims.

approvalRequestId and originatingPayloadSha256 must match a prior immutable People-owned waiver-request fence for the same tenant, case, task, maker, requester, reason, task owner revision, task version, exact APR-002 request bytes, request body digest, request payload digest, command digest and correlationId.

decisionRevision in the body must equal the signed ownerRevision claim; each approvalRequestId is its own stream whose first and only terminal decision revision is 1, exact delivery replay is a no-op, and a later waiver attempt requires a new approvalRequestId with a new revision-1 stream.
People independently revalidates that decisionActorPublicId differs from both the immutable caseMakerPublicId and requestedByActorPublicId before any waiver effect.

APPROVED changes an eligible PENDING, IN_PROGRESS or FAILED task to WAIVED only when every step-up evidence field is non-null, exactly body/proof aligned, fresh, single-use, audience-bound and purpose-bound.
REJECTED is protocol-accepted evidence but never mutates the task to WAIVED, never satisfies a mandatory task, and all step-up evidence fields and claims must be absent rather than null.
An APPROVED final mandatory-task waiver can move TASKS_ACTIVE to READY_TO_PUBLISH under the same aggregate CAS; it is the previously missing waiver transition.
A waiver cannot clear or override irreversibleAt and cannot waive a task already COMPLETED.
The concrete path casePublicId equals the body and signed JWT claims.
The case must be PUBLISHED and the caller must hold an admitted XCON-028 consumer fence for the exact event identity and payload digest.
ownerRevision is monotonic per tenant, case and caller; first is 1 and every distinct accepted result is exactly previous accepted revision plus 1.
CONSISTENT appends accepted evidence and leaves PUBLISHED unchanged.
CORRECTION_REQUIRED atomically advances PUBLISHED to CORRECTION_REQUIRED under exact People aggregate CAS and never edits the published event.
A later correction or rehire is a linked new intent; it cannot publish a duplicate WorkerSeparated event for the original case.
The HRIS-PER consumer uses the same closed SeparationReconciliationResultV1 semantics and tenant context.
The port requires the exact PUBLISHED XCON-028 identity and digest and applies the same replay, revision, audit and CAS rules.
It grants no HRIS-PER implementation, subscription or completion authority in this carrier.

common.occurredAtRule: occurredAt must not precede the immutable protocol-fence created_at and must not be more than 5 seconds after owner receipt time. A long transport delay is allowed when the event still matches the exact next revision and digest; JWT freshness is evaluated independently per delivery attempt.

SeparationTaskReceiptV2.originatingPayloadRule: originatingPayloadSha256 exactly equals the immutable task-dispatch payload digest recorded by People before the owner was permitted to execute the task.
SeparationTaskReceiptV2.deltaReason: The V61 task invariant requires an immutable external receipt identity as durable callback evidence, and a FAILED-to-COMPLETED successor must prove a different external receipt.

rules: decisionRevision exactly equals ownerRevision in the body and the signed ownerRevision workload-proof claim.
originatingPayloadSha256 exactly equals approval_request_payload_sha256 in the immutable People APR-002 request outbox/fence.

For APPROVED, stepUpEvidenceDigest binds approvalRequestId, decisionActorPublicId, stepUpEvidenceAudience, stepUpEvidencePurpose, stepUpEvidenceNonce and stepUpVerifiedAt; Approval atomically consumes that one-time nonce before terminal decision and records stepUpConsumedAt.

For APPROVED, stepUpVerifiedAt is not after stepUpConsumedAt, stepUpConsumedAt is not after occurredAt, and both fall within the frozen workflow freshness policy; People verifies exact body/JWT/outbox equality and rejects evidence identity, nonce or digest reuse.
For REJECTED, step-up evidence is not required and every step-up field and claim is absent; explicit null is invalid under the closed schema.
SeparationWaiverDecisionV2.deltaReason: The v1 body could not distinguish approval from rejection, bind the originating APR-002 payload, prove independent maker/requester checks or carry single-use step-up evidence, and could not therefore prove an approval-authorized WAIVED transition.

SeparationReconciliationResultV1.taskPublicIdRule: Not present and not part of this callback type's digest or persistence mapping; separation_task_id is null for RECONCILIATION_RESULT.
SeparationReconciliationResultV1.originatingPayloadRule: originatingPayloadSha256 exactly equals the immutable XCON-028 WorkerSeparated.v1 published-event payload digest admitted for the caller.

canonicalDigestRules.payloadSha256: Lowercase SHA-256 of RFC 8785 canonical JSON containing the exact request schema name, its declared version (2 for SeparationTaskReceiptV2 and SeparationWaiverDecisionV2; 1 for SeparationReconciliationResultV1), and every request body field except payloadSha256. Trusted transport context is not part of this business payload digest.
canonicalDigestRules.originatingPayloadSha256: A separate immutable dispatch-lineage digest, never the callback self payloadSha256: task-dispatch payload for HRM-008, admitted XCON-028 WorkerSeparated.v1 event payload for HRM-009, and People APR-002 request payload_sha256 persisted as approval_request_payload_sha256 for HRM-010. It is required in every callback body and signed workload proof.
canonicalDigestRules.requestBodySha256: Lowercase SHA-256 of the exact received UTF-8 request bytes after transport decompression; content encodings are forbidden.
canonicalDigestRules.commandDigestEncoding: The nine values above are encoded in that order as UTF-8 with one LF delimiter and no trailing LF, then SHA-256 lowercase hexadecimal.
canonicalDigestRules.pathBodyEquality: Path identities and body identities are compared before owner lookup and are also exact JWT claims.
canonicalDigestRules.correlationRule: X-Correlation-ID, JWT correlationId and body correlationId are the same canonical lowercase UUID; the initiating People outbox owns it and callers cannot replace it.

SVC-PEP-HRM-010.decisionRevisionRule: decisionRevision is required in the body but deliberately not duplicated as a JWT claim; it must exactly equal the signed ownerRevision claim.

jwt.strictness: Unknown, duplicate, missing, blank, coerced, noncanonical or mismatched protected headers or claims fail before replay reservation and owner facts. For HRM-010 the exact claim set is the always-required set plus the APPROVED conditional set, or the always-required set with all step-up claims absent for REJECTED.

requiredApplicationHeaders.X-DWP-Service-Identity: exactly one exact caller workload ID
requiredApplicationHeaders.X-Correlation-ID: exactly one canonical lowercase UUID equal to body and JWT

headerRules: Duplicate required or forbidden headers are rejected rather than joined.
Tenant, caller, audience, purpose, case, task, revision and digest headers never create authority.
Content-Encoding and Transfer-Encoding transformations are forbidden at the application boundary.

rules: The owner loads a current ACTIVE service grant by the signed key and does not accept a request-derived fallback.
The target case and optional task belong to the same signed tenant under forced RLS.
The callback caller, purpose and task type equal the immutable protocol fence created when People dispatched that exact work.
A browser principal, delegated user, support session, gateway assertion or tenant header contributes no authority.
Feature OFF, missing grant, stale revision, unavailable trust state or ambiguous identity fails closed.

guardOrder: Validate TLS 1.3, the client certificate chain, exact single SPIFFE URI SAN and revocation state.
Validate method, concrete path shape, no query or alias, body size, media types and the strict header allowlist/denylist.

Validate compact JWS structure, key, signature, closed claims, certificate confirmation, issuer, subject, audience, times, tenant, binding, purpose, path identities, revision, correlation and exact body hash.

Load only current service-authority metadata, verify jti and requestNonce are distinct, derive their separate token digests, then atomically insert both tenant-scoped rows into the one security replay namespace.

Check the callback identity ledger by tenantId, callerWorkloadId and callbackEventId; exact command digest returns the stored response without owner fact reads, while a conflict returns 409 and appends quarantine audit without changing the existing row.

Check the immutable ppl_separation_callback_authorities fence for exact caller, binding, purpose, case, optional task, expected next owner revision, correlation and originating payload digest; for HRM-010 also check the immutable ppl_separation_waiver_request_outbox fence before any aggregate business read.
Only then resolve and lock the minimum same-tenant case and optional task identities, verify lifecycle and People aggregate CAS, and read no unrelated worker facts.
Atomically persist callback evidence, callback-specific state effect, receipt_public_id, exact safe SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 bytes, audit and any outbox result; rollback all on failure.

protocolFenceRequirement.purpose: Make caller ownership, expected revision and dispatch lineage verifiable before aggregate reads.
protocolFenceRequirement.createdBy: dwp-people-server owner transaction that dispatches or admits the exact work
protocolFenceRequirement.streamNullSemantics: The unique stream key uses NULLS NOT DISTINCT. approval_request_id is non-null only for HRM-010; it is null for HRM-008 and HRM-009.

columnSemantics.expected_next_owner_revision: The only ownerRevision admissible for this exact immutable stream key; every new stream starts at 1 and subsequent distinct callbacks in that same stream require the exact next revision.
columnSemantics.correlation_id: Equals body, X-Correlation-ID and signed correlationId.
columnSemantics.originating_payload_sha256: Equals the signed originatingPayloadSha256: task dispatch for HRM-008, XCON-028 event for HRM-009, and People APR-002 request payload for HRM-010.
columnSemantics.task_type: Required for HRM-008 and HRM-010; null only for HRM-009.
columnSemantics.approval_request_id: Required only for HRM-010, equals its immutable People waiver-request outbox identity and is part of the revision stream key; null for HRM-008 and HRM-009.
columnSemantics.consumer_event_id: Required only for HRM-009 and equals the admitted XCON-028 event identity; null for HRM-008 and HRM-010.
columnSemantics.tenant_grant_revision: Equals the signed tenantGrantRevision and the current People service-grant row used for this binding, caller and purpose.
columnSemantics.authorization_revision: Equals the separately signed authorizationRevision and the same current People service-grant row; it is never inferred from tenant_grant_revision.
columnSemantics.created_at: Immutable owner timestamp recorded in the dispatch/admission transaction and the lower bound for callback occurredAt.
columnSemantics.closed_at: Null for an open ADMIT authority; closure is represented by an append-only successor authority row carrying closed_at, never an update to the original row.

rules: task_public_id is non-null for HRM-008 and HRM-010 and null only for HRM-009.
approval_request_id is a stream-key column rather than a repeated required-value column; it is non-null only for HRM-010.
tenant_grant_revision and authorization_revision are separate values from the same current service-grant row and both equal their signed claims.

For HRM-010 each new approval_request_id creates a new stream whose first ownerRevision and decisionRevision are 1; the terminal APPROVED or REJECTED decision closes that request stream and no later revision is admitted.
A later waiver attempt must create a new approvalRequestId and therefore a new stream beginning at revision 1; revision continuity never crosses approval requests.
An application cache or mutable configuration row is insufficient.
The separately sealed People V61 manifest successor must allocate this exact table and column semantics before migration authoring.
People creates the row atomically with the APR-002 outbox under exact task CAS before any Approval submission.
exact_request_body is the immutable UTF-8 APR-002 request bytes capped at 32768 bytes; it is never emitted to logs, metrics or errors.

request_body_sha256 binds exact_request_body; approval_request_payload_sha256 binds the canonical request payload; command_digest binds the APR-002 method, path, caller, audience, tenant, purpose, media type and request body digest.
HRM-010 must exactly match every identity, reason, revision, version, originating digest and correlation value before aggregate reads.
People independently rejects HRM-010 when decision_actor_public_id equals either case_maker_public_id or requested_by_actor_public_id.

reservationRows.tokenDigest: lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical UTF-8 jti
lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical UTF-8 requestNonce

rules: jti and requestNonce are distinct canonical UUIDs and therefore their token_digest values must differ.
Both tenant-scoped token-digest rows are inserted atomically into the same namespace before protocol-fence or aggregate reads; one collision rolls back both reservations.
Uniqueness is tenant_id plus token_digest, so reuse is rejected even when a later proof changes binding_id, caller_workload_id or token_kind.
APR-002 applies the identical two-row rule in the separately sealed Approval V59 apr_hrm013_proof_replays namespace.

replayAndPersistence.sameCallbackSameCommandDigest: Return the original byte-identical stored response with no aggregate read or mutation; REPLAY_NOOP is telemetry only and the persisted callback outcome is unchanged.
replayAndPersistence.sameCallbackDifferentCommandDigest: Return 409 with no existence detail, preserve the original callback row and response, append a separate QUARANTINED audit event, and perform no aggregate read or mutation.
replayAndPersistence.newCallback: Require exact next owner revision from the protocol fence and process in one owner transaction.
requiredDurableEvidence: decision and decisionRevision for approval callbacks
all seven step-up evidence fields for approved waiver callbacks
replayAndPersistence.migrationRule: The v1 People V61 manifest is insufficient for this evidence. An append-only manifest successor must add these fields and the protocol fence before any V61 reservation or SQL authoring.

conditionalFields.taskPublicId: Required and non-null for TASK_RECEIPT and APPROVAL_DECISION; absent for RECONCILIATION_RESULT.

retryable: transport failure before a verified response
retryContract.responseSizeRule: Any response over 16384 bytes is unverifiable, is never interpreted as success and follows the bounded invalid-receipt retry path.
retryContract.senderRule: A sender never invents success after timeout and never changes the request body or callback identity while retrying.

metrics: callback latency and status by binding and caller

minimumCorrections: Add append-only ppl_separation_callback_authorities with the exact protocol-fence column names and semantics in this carrier.
Add ppl_hrm013_callback_proof_replays for callback jti/requestNonce reservations and ppl_separation_waiver_request_outbox for the immutable People APR-002 request fence.
Persist command_digest and request_body_sha256 without storing raw request bytes.
Persist originating_payload_sha256 separately from callback payload_sha256.
Persist receipt_public_id, exact safe SeparationCallbackReceiptV1 bytes capped at 16384 bytes and response_body_sha256 for byte-identical replay without reusing generic ppl_command_receipts.
Persist approval_request_id, decision, decision_revision and all seven conditional step-up evidence fields for approval callbacks.
Bind external_receipt_public_id as durable callback evidence for every task receipt status.
Keep callback rows and terminal response evidence immutable under forced tenant RLS.

pairedApprovalRequestBinding.reason: SVC-PEP-APR-001 is fixed to employee-change approval semantics and cannot be reused without purpose confusion.
pairedApprovalRequestBinding.rule: The sibling append-only successor seals the request path, schema, workflow and Approval V59 touch manifest. After this carrier is independently reviewed and pushed, separate hash-bound tokens may authorize the central Approval V59 bridge and only the bounded People V61 prerequisite persistence; both must integrate before an HRM-013 module owner packet or module source token.

acceptanceConditions: Exactly the three callback ingress bindings HRM-008 through HRM-010 exist, and none is browser, gateway or public OpenAPI reachable.
Only the exact caller SPIFFE identity, RS256 key, audience, purpose, signed tenant and current service grant reach callback protocol metadata.
Path, body, JWT and correlation identities match exactly, while unknown, duplicate, additional, coerced or oversized input fails closed.
Task callers can report only their exact canonical task type and exact next owner revision.

A waiver APPROVED decision requires the exact immutable APR-002 request bytes/digests, a decision actor different from both maker and requester, exact decisionRevision-to-signed-ownerRevision equality, and seven fresh single-use step-up evidence fields aligned across body, proof and outbox; REJECTED carries no step-up fields and never waives.
CONSISTENT reconciliation preserves PUBLISHED while CORRECTION_REQUIRED appends the state transition without editing the published event.
Exact callback replay returns the stored byte-identical response without aggregate reads; digest conflict preserves the original row and quarantines by audit.
Spoofed authority and protocol mismatch fail before business facts; a new valid callback uses minimum identity-only owner reads and exact CAS before mutation.

No raw callback body, worker PII or sensitive payload is stored or logged; only the bounded immutable APR-002 request outbox retains exact request bytes, while the safe callback receipt and cryptographic digests are durable.
HRIS-PER uses a typed in-process port and never self-HTTP; no consumer subscription is activated.
The People V61 manifest correction and paired Approval request binding remain explicit blockers before module source.
Feature state remains OFF with zero tenant enrollment, runtime credentials, production binding and business completion credit.
nonClaims: The three callback endpoints, protocol fence, schemas or handlers are implemented.
SVC-PEP-APR-002 or its paired HRM-010 callback is implemented or runtime-authorized.
The v1 People V61 manifest is sufficient without an append-only successor.
People V61 or its bounded prerequisite persistence is reserved, leased, authored or executed.
An HRM-013 owner packet, module worktree or executable source token exists.
Runtime keys, certificates, tenant grants, callback senders or production credentials are configured.
XCON-028 production publication or a TIM, PAY or PER consumer subscription is active.
The HRM-013 page or menu is mounted, enabled or tenant-enrolled.
HRM-013, Batch-06 or HRIS is complete.
